text:
marc: Heads-up — deploying v2.14.0 to prod in the 02:00 UTC window. Main change is the adaptive-routing flag. Planning a soft-vent ramp + pin/unpin fallback.

jenna: Thanks. Can you paste the exact flag config we'll use? Want to ensure targeting is clear.

marc: Pasted below (also added to release notes):
```json
{
  "feature": "adaptive_routing_v2",
  "initial_pct": 2,
  "ramp_schedule": [2,10,35,75],
  "ramp_intervals_min": [15,20,30,60],
  "pinned_version": "v2.14.0",
  "fallback": "route_v1"
}
```

marc: Key ops: start at 2% (canary cohort), hold 15m, then 10% -> 35% -> 75% with progressive holdpoints. If any latency or error delta > 3% we fast-unpin to route_v1.

deploy-bot: CI checks passed. Deploy queue: queued for prod-02. ETA ~30m.

sre-oncall: I'll watch p95 latency and error budget. Set alerts at +2.5% p95 and +1% error-rate. If we hit either, we'll pause ramp and hold.

carla: Obs note — please enable token-level tracing for 30m on canary cohort (sampling 10/1000) so we can trace regressions quickly.

marc: Will enable tracing and add a short-term debug log level. Also toggling KV-cache warmup to avoid cold-start thrash.

jenna: Release notes snippet ready. Including rollback steps and contact.

product-ops: FYI — marketing will see a small UX tweak for 10% of users at the 10% step. Confirmed no user-visible A/B swap apart from latency differences.

marc: Quick rollback checklist (pinned in thread):
- /deploy rollback v2.14.0 (this will unpin and route to fallback)
- If deploy-bot unresponsive: toggle flag to "off" in FF console and set pinned_version to "route_v1"
- Notify #incidents and start postmortem if >30m degradation

jenna: Who has permission to force-unpin during window?

marc: jenna, sre-oncall, and carla are listed as emergency unpin. deploy-bot will still accept ops commands.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: v2.14.0 -> prod (canary target 2%). Build 8345. Logs: https://ci.redwood/in/8345

sre-oncall: Canary 2% live. p95: 120ms (baseline 115ms), errors: 0.02% (baseline 0.015%). Watching.

carla: Tracing logs enabled. Sharing link to trace dashboard.

marc: Holdpoint for 15m. If all good, increase to 10%.

jenna: LGTM from product side.

sre-oncall: 7m in — p95 drift now +0.6%, errors +0.01%. Continuing.

deploy-bot: User traffic shifted to 10% (step 2).

sre-oncall: At 10% — p95 +1.8%, errors +0.9% (within threshold). Plan to continue to 35% after 20m.

marc: Note: if small oscillation appears at 35% we should slow intervals (double hold time) rather than roll back immediately.

product-ops: Confirmed — don't flip UX experiments yet at 35% until 1hr soak.

sre-oncall: At 35% step: p95 +3.5% (threshold exceeded). Pausing ramp, escalating.

marc: Acknowledged. Pausing ramp. Initiating fast-unpin plan: switching traffic back to route_v1 for affected cohorts.

jenna: Sending customer comms hold note.

deploy-bot: Executing emergency unpin: updating feature flag to fallback and setting pinned_version=route_v1. Command logged.

sre-oncall: Post-action metrics: p95 back to +0.4%, errors back to baseline. All cohorts stable.

carla: Collected traces look like KV-cache pressure at 30–40%—need follow-up on warmup heuristics.

marc: Good catch. We'll hold release and open follow-up issue for runtime cache tuning + a test that simulates 40% load.

product-ops: Notifying stakeholders and putting rollout back to TBD.

marc: Summary: successful soft-vent run — canary caught regression, safe fast-unpin worked. Next steps: tune cache warmup, adjust ramp schedule (slower from 10->35), and re-run in next maintenance window.

jenna: Thanks everyone. Adding retro notes and scheduling postmortem if we need deeper investigation.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished with status: ROLLBACK_EXECUTED. Refer to logs: https://ci.redwood/in/8345/rollback
